pick.headline: North Korea announces NPT withdrawal
pick.summary: On March 12, 1993, North Korea announced its intention to withdraw from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty after the IAEA demanded special inspections.
pick.significance: It opened the first North Korean nuclear crisis, which brought the peninsula close to war before the 1994 Agreed Framework.
pick.fbis: The East Asia Daily Report of March 12, 1993, carried Tokyo KYODO: Foreign Minister Watanabe called North Korea's NPT withdrawal a "challenge" to nonproliferation that "creates a grave situation", and a spokesman said a strike on Yongbyon was premature to discuss.

alternates.headline: Serial bombings in Bombay
alternates.summary: On March 12, 1993, a series of bombs exploded across Bombay, killing about 250 people.
alternates.significance: India accused Pakistani intelligence of involvement; the attacks were organized by Dawood Ibrahim's criminal network.
alternates.fbis: The Near East & South Asia Daily Report of March 15, 1993, carried Delhi All India Radio on 12 explosions across Bombay, the heaviest at the Stock Exchange, with police counting 174 dead and over 940 injured, and Chief Minister Pawar calling it an attempt to destabilize India's economy.
